architecture.ai_summary:
Liza is a Go CLI orchestration system centered on a file-backed blackboard. cmd/liza parses and routes user requests into internal/commands; commands perform CLI-level validation and formatting; internal/ops owns durable task, agent, review, merge, worktree, indexing, and state mutations. internal/models defines the shared schema, internal/db serializes blackboard access with locks and watchers, and internal/statevalidate enforces schema, artifact, dependency, sprint, role, and pipeline invariants.

Agent execution is driven by configurable role pipelines. internal/pipeline defines role pairs, states, transitions, review policies, context sections, and timeouts; internal/agent claims tasks, builds prompts through internal/prompts, runs provider CLIs, maintains leases and heartbeats, masks secrets, and invokes support systems such as pre-commit, git, Stacklit, SCIP, Semble, and functional-clusters when enabled.

Cross-cutting infrastructure is kept in narrow packages: git/gitenv wrap repository commands, paths centralizes artifact locations, process/procscan manage agent processes, envgate gates optional capabilities, secretmask protects logs and prompts, and jsonout/render/tui/log/alerts expose operator feedback. Most feature work should preserve this boundary: CLI surface in cmd/liza and internal/commands, business behavior in internal/ops, data shape in internal/models, and lifecycle protection in pipeline and state validation.
